description: A key introduces itself: its public key, what kind of thing holds it, and how it is kept. Signed by that key, so the record proves the holder has it. It claims nothing about authority.

custody.description: How the private key is kept, as the holder states it: for example hardware, kms, host, software.

details.description: Issuer-defined detail: up to 64 named scalars. Nothing in it is interpreted by the base kinds, and nothing in it is content; content goes behind a reference.

holder.description: What holds the key. Open: an issuer may use other words.

identity.description: A stable identity written as a URI. Syntax is not authentication.

publicKey.description: A public key: a registered algorithm and the key's bytes in strict padded base64.
